facts.text: Allakhazam's bestiary lists the Chthonic Knights of Darkness Falls.
Several names echo the Ars Goetia: Marbas (5) for Marbos, Gaap (33) for Gaapoler, Haagenti (48) for Haag, Zagan (61) for Zagal, Ronove (27) for Ronoro, Orobas (55) for Obarus; to verify for each.
Ukobat may read as Ukobach, the stoker of hell's fires in de Plancy, and Tamuel as Tamiel, a Watcher of Enoch; to verify.
The oath, the posts and the chapter roll are Living Server lore.

story:
The Chthonic Knights are Prince Abdin's order, the Blade, and the court's oldest soldiery. Abdin founded them in the First Roll in his quarter of the hollow, the north-west, where the rock is hardest and the warm air from the deep fires least reaches. The first knights knelt on the floor of the chapter house and took an oath to the deep earth itself: to hold what is taken whole, and to go down rather than give ground. They wear one shape, plated and black, made for standing, and they have stood in it since. Every knight of the order keeps a post, and a knight is known by where it stands; the realms that have walked the hollow say they have never yet found a knight anywhere but where the last one stood.

The order's history is a history of quarrels. Abdin and Prince Asmoien both claimed to have knelt second at the Feast of Thrones, and Grand Chancellor Adremal wrote them on one line. From that line came the order's great enemy, Asmoien's Mutilators, the Hook, and the feud of the Blade and the Hook, which broke out in the Fourth Roll and ended at the central crossing when Gatekeeper Dommel closed every road out of it and let the two orders kill each other until neither mattered. Since then knights stand at the Gate beside Mutilators and Inquisitors, sworn to draw no blade there, and the chapter counts the Gate oath the hardest it asks of anyone.

The chapter has given knights away and lost them. It lent knights to the Field Marshal after the feud, and they stand at the east arch of High Lord Baln's hall to this day, unsure whose they are. It gave four of its best to the Master, who keeps them on the approach as Legion's Own. It sent a garrison to Duke Bimure's East Ward between the eastern halls, and from that garrison High Lord Saeor took the knight Zepor, who is a duke now and the Oathbreaker of the chapter roll. The chapter sends a champion east against him each Roll; none has made him yield. It lost a knight called Mermer to the Inquisition in the feud, and does not say his name. It keeps the Marshal's officer, Lieutenant Persun, in its house, and has never decided whether he is a guest.

The chapter house stands on Earl Glassalab's tunnels, and the knights know it. Their prince's plans run through those tunnels now, toward Director Kobil's chambers above the Gate and the Army of Shadows. The knights do not like the Army. A shadow cannot hold ground, they say, because it does not know where the ground is.

The realms have their own names for them. Albion's knights call them the Black Order and argue about whether a demon can keep an oath; Midgard's huscarls respect them more than anything else below the world, because they stand; Hibernia's champions say they are the oldest kind of geis-bound warrior, sworn to the earth instead of to a king, and that the earth keeps them.
legend: The Chthonic Knights are spread across the whole dungeon, always in the same posts: three with Prince Abdin in the north-west (Gaapoler, Haag, Vosoes), six in the chapter house (Absax, Azea, Zagal, Ronoro, Ukobat, Ezpeth), four of Legion's Own on the approach (Fonath, Carabia, Olov, Tamuel), three at the east arch of Baln's hall (Marbos, Zaeber, Exal), six in the East Ward camps (Aciel, Ain, Babyzu, Carnivon, Prosel, Zafan) and three at the Gate (Exte, Ibeko, Obarus). Levels run 60 to 74, all slashing melee, no scripts. They do not wander; every knight is exactly where the last one was, so you can plan a route. Most come back in about three minutes, but the guard, the chapter house elders and Fonath take half an hour. Players call them the black knights and pull them one camp at a time.

loremasterTopic.text: Prince [Abdin]'s order, the Blade, sworn to the deep earth to hold what is taken and go down rather than give ground. They fought the [Mutilators] in the feud of the Blade and the Hook; they stand at the Gate, in the East Ward, in Baln's hall and on the Master's approach, and they keep the chapter roll of the champions sent against Duke [Zepor].

bookPage: From a Midgard huscarl's account, told in the longhouse at Jordheim: I have stood in a shield-wall. I know what it is to set your feet. The black knights below set theirs as if the floor had grown up around them. We came on them in the north-west, at the door of their prince, and they did not step forward to meet us and they did not step back. We broke on them like a wave on a skerry. One of them had worn two hollows into the floor in front of the door, and when he fell at last he fell into them, standing, and his feet are there still.
bookPages: From a Midgard huscarl's account, told in the longhouse at Jordheim: I have stood in a shield-wall. I know what it is to set your feet. The black knights below set theirs as if the floor had grown up around them. We came on them in the north-west, at the door of their prince, and they did not step forward to meet us and they did not step back. We broke on them like a wave on a skerry. One of them had worn two hollows into the floor in front of the door, and when he fell at last he fell into them, standing, and his feet are there still.

The huscarl went on: Their house is further in, and there is a knight inside who says names. We heard him through the door before we went in, a long list, each name followed by the same words, and then one name with nothing after it. Our skald said he had heard of an oath that is sworn to the earth instead of to a jarl. I asked him what happens to a man who breaks it. He said the earth does not forget, and that the knight with no words after his name was somewhere in the east, standing on ground that would not have him.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Fonath
members.story: Fonath is the eldest knight of Legion's Own and the strongest knight on the Roll. When the Master asked Prince Abdin for knights to stand on the approach, Abdin sent the best he had, reasoning that a knight given to the Master would still remember the chapter house. Fonath remembers it, and has never once gone back. He stands nearest the door of the four, below the Chamberlain.

aggro: The Master's knight. Kneel, or fall.
death: The ground... held...

lairEntry: A knight stands at the foot of the slope as if rooted.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Carabia
members.story: Carabia stands beside Fonath at the bottom of the approach and carries the knights' banner of the deep earth, a strip of black stone hung on a chain. The imps say the banner was cut from the floor of the chapter house on the day the four were given to the Master, so that the floor of the north-west would always be where they stood.

aggro: The deep earth is under you. It is not on your side.
death: Carry the stone... back...

lairEntry: A banner of black stone hangs on a chain, unmoving.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Olov
members.story: Olov was the youngest of the four given to the Master, and the court remembers him for one thing: on his first day on the slope he asked the Chamberlain whom he was guarding the door from. The Chamberlain told him. Olov has stood on the approach since without asking anything else, a little up the slope from Fonath and Carabia.

aggro: I asked once whom I guard against. Now I know.
death: Tell the chapter... I asked nothing more...

lairEntry: A young knight's shape stands very straight on the slope.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Tamuel
members.story: Tamuel keeps the upper end of Legion's Own, nearest the Chancellor's table and Earl Vone. He is the only knight who can read the walls of the approach, having been taught by the Archivist before he took his oath, and the Chancellor dislikes him for it. Tamuel says nothing about what he reads. He reads the newest wall every Roll, and then stands a little straighter.

aggro: Your realm is on the wall. I have read it.
death: Read my line... to the chapter...
slay: One more line for the wall.

lairEntry: A knight is reading the walls of the approach.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Gaapoler
members.story: Gaapoler is the second knight to bear the name. The first was Prince Abdin's champion, who fought Duke Eligar to the yield over precedence on the stair and knelt; the present Gaapoler took the name and the post at Abdin's door, and has asked Eligar for the return fight every Roll since. Eligar has said he will fight the next one, and Gaapoler intends there to be no next one.

aggro: I am Gaapoler. The second. Not the last.
death: Tell Eligar... the rematch stands...

lairEntry: Before the prince's hall a champion waits for someone else.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Haag
members.story: Haag is the prince's shield-knight and the one knight of the guard who stands nearest Earl Glassalab, which the others consider a kind of courage. He keeps the prince's hall the old way, by never moving from it. The chapter house says Haag's feet have worn two hollows in the floor before Abdin's door, and that the earl has dug carefully around them.

aggro: The prince's door. I have not moved from it in ten Rolls.
death: Two hollows... in the floor... keep them...

lairEntry: Two hollows are worn into the floor before the door.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Vosoes
members.story: Vosoes is the youngest of Abdin's guard and its messenger, the only one of the three allowed to leave the door. He carries the prince's word to the chapter house and to the Director's chambers above the Gate. The imps say he has walked Earl Glassalab's tunnel to the Director and back, and that he will not say how long it is.

aggro: The prince sent me. He sends me everywhere.
death: The tunnel... do not tell the Gatekeeper...

lairEntry: A knight waits by the prince's hall, ready to be sent.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Absax
members.story: Absax is the master of the chapter house, the knight who says the chapter roll aloud: the champions who went east against the Oathbreaker, one after another, and then the Oathbreaker's own name, and then nothing. He stands with Knight Ronoro at the inner door. It is Absax who chooses each Roll's champion, and the chapter notes that he has never chosen himself.

aggro: Kneel to the deep earth or go into it.
death: Say my name... after the others...

lairEntry: A voice inside the chapter house is reciting names.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Azea
members.story: Azea keeps the chapter house's outer approach, toward Princess Nahemah's bower, and is the knight the bower has tried hardest to turn. The bower sent her a face she had loved in the Uncounted Age, and then another, and then a third. Azea has looked at each and told it to go home. The chapter considers her the proof that the oath holds.

aggro: Show me another face. I will not look at it either.
death: The oath... held... to the end...

lairEntry: Faint perfume hangs here. The knight ignores it.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Zagal
members.story: Zagal is the chapter's keeper of oaths, who hears each new knight swear to the deep earth and keeps the words. He stands among the newest knights of the house, a little apart, and he is said to be the quietest demon in the north-west: Zagal does not challenge, does not call, and does not wake for small things.

aggro: You woke me. That was unwise.
death: The oath... is kept... without me...

lairEntry: A knight stands in the chapter house as if asleep.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Ronoro
members.story: Ronoro stands at the inner door of the chapter house with Absax and teaches the newest knights to stand. That is all he teaches: where to put their feet, and how not to move them. The young knights call him the Mason, after Marquis Sabonach, and say Ronoro builds knights the way the marquis builds arches.

aggro: Feet. Watch my feet. They do not move.
death: Stand... someone stand in my place...

lairEntry: Bootmarks are cut into the stone of the chapter floor.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Ukobat
members.story: Ukobat keeps the chapter house's fires, the braziers by which the knights take their oath, and he is the only knight of the house who is never cold. The chapter says he was a stoker in the Uncounted Age, feeding the deep fires under Baelerdoth's hall, and that he came west to the knights when Duke Harboris first started taking the fire for himself.

aggro: Closer to the fire. It is the last warm thing you will feel.
death: Let the braziers... go out...

lairEntry: Braziers burn hot in the chapter house. Someone tends them.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Ezpeth
members.story: Ezpeth keeps the high end of the chapter house, the climb toward Princess Nahemah's bower, and watches the bower for the chapter. She sees Ambassador Mannam go up the Albion stair and come back, and counts his journeys on a cord. The chapter has asked her to stop counting; the cord is now longer than she is tall.

aggro: Another visitor from the stair. I will count you.
death: My cord... finish it...

lairEntry: A knotted cord hangs from a peg, very long.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Marbos
members.post: the Field Marshal's knights, Baln's hall
members.story: Marbos commands the knights the Field Marshal keeps in Baln's hall, at the east arch near the war table. The chapter lent them to Nebir after the feud of the Blade and the Hook, and Marbos has never quite decided whether he serves the prince or the Marshal. He settles it each day by standing exactly halfway between the arch and the table.

aggro: Prince or Marshal? Neither will save you.
death: Halfway... I stood halfway...

members.name: Chthonic Knight Zaeber
members.post: the Field Marshal's knights, Baln's hall
members.story: Zaeber stands with Marbos at the east arch of Baln's hall. He is the Marshal's favourite among the lent knights, because he is the only one who can stand perfectly still while Nebir counts him, and the Marshal has written to the chapter twice asking to keep him. The chapter has twice said no, and Zaeber has not been asked what he thinks.

aggro: Count me, then. I will not move.
death: The Marshal... will want the number...

lairEntry: Two knights guard the east arch. One does not even breathe.

members.post: the Field Marshal's knights, Baln's hall
members.story: Exal keeps the far side of the Marshal's knights, toward the East Ward, and is the one who carries word between Nebir's table and Duke Bimure's garrison. The Ward knights call him the Marshal's knight and the Marshal calls him the Ward's, and Exal has given up correcting either.

aggro: The Marshal sends his regards. So does the Ward.
death: Tell the Ward... tell the Marshal...

lairEntry: A knight waits on the road from the war table to the Ward.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Aciel
members.story: Aciel is the youngest knight of the East Ward and keeps its northern edge near High Lord Oro's hall. He is the only knight in the Ward who has spoken to Duke Sallis, who asked him, the first night, which of the three Oros he thought was real. Aciel said he was a knight and would guard all three. Sallis has been fond of him since.

aggro: I guard all three. You will not reach any of them.
death: All three... I guarded all three...

lairEntry: A young knight at the Ward's edge faces three doors.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Ain
members.story: Ain stands with the Ward's middle camp. In the Sixth Roll he stood beside Zepor on the last watch before Zepor went east to High Lord Saeor, and Earl Oraxus touched Zepor's shoulder over Ain's. Ain has never forgiven the earl for choosing the other knight, which the chapter considers the wrong grudge to hold.

aggro: Saeor's taster passed me over. You will not.
death: He chose Zepor... he should have chosen...

lairEntry: A knight of the Ward glares east, toward Saeor's hall.

members.name: Chthonic Knight Babyzu
members.story: Babyzu keeps the Ward's north-western corner, where its ground meets the road from the Gate. He is the Ward's oldest knight and the only one who has served there since the First Roll, and Duke Bimure trusts him with the worst of the duty: standing between the high lords' followers when they come out of their halls to quarrel.

aggro: Between. Always between.
death: Who stands between now...

members.name: Chthonic Knight Carnivon
members.story: Carnivon stands near Duke Bimure's end of the Ward, close to High Lord Baelerdoth's door, and is the knight the Ward sends to stand nearest the high lord's thirst. He has no ward left to lose, the others say, and so he goes where wards are drunk. He is said to have laughed once, in the Fifth Roll, and nobody knows at what.

aggro: Nothing left to drink. Come and see.
death: Dry... at last...

members.story: Prosel keeps the Ward's middle ground with Zafan and Ain, and keeps the Ward's dead: when a knight of the Ward falls in a quarrel between the halls, Prosel carries it to the Mutilators, and then stands watch until the Mutilators have finished. The Ward says he is the only knight who can bear to watch the Hook at work.

aggro: I carry the fallen. I will carry you.
death: Carry me... to the knights, not the Hook...

members.name: Chthonic Knight Zafan
members.story: Zafan is the senior knight of the Ward and its oldest rival of Duke Zepor. He served beside Zepor in the first garrison and has been chosen as the chapter's champion against him once already; he came back, which no other champion has done, and will not say how. The chapter has not chosen him again.

aggro: I came back from the Oathbreaker. I will come back from you.
death: Tell Absax... I came back once...

members.story: Exte keeps the Gate's western road with the Mutilator Okabi, and is the knight who takes the oath of the Gate each Roll: to keep the crossing with the other two orders and to draw no blade against them there. He finds the oath harder than any he swore in the chapter house, and says so to Okabi every day.

aggro: The Gatekeeper's toll. Pay it to me.
death: The watch... is short a knight...

members.story: Ibeko keeps the Gate's northern side and is the watch's memory: he was a knight of the first Gate watch, after the Blade and the Hook, and remembers the crossing when it was full of the dead of both orders. He alone of the watch still looks at the Mutilators with open hatred, and Gatekeeper Dommel is said to like him for it.

death: Full again...
